uneven-pay.name: Uneven pay
uneven-pay.line: My pay changes so much from month to month that I can't plan.
aliases: Income that goes up and down

sources.passage: In 2024, 11 percent of adults reported they struggled to pay their bills in the prior 12 months because their income varied

uneven-pay.prevalence: In 2024, 11 percent of U.S. adults struggled to pay bills because their income varied (Federal Reserve SHED).

cant-get-credit.name: Credit
cant-get-credit.line: I get turned down when I need a loan or a credit card.

sources.passage: Among those who applied, one-third were either denied credit or approved for less credit than they requested.
Access to credit

cant-get-credit.prevalence: Of U.S. adults who applied for credit, one-third were denied or approved for less (Federal Reserve SHED). Ipsos tracks access to credit as a national worry.

no-bank-account.name: Bank account
no-bank-account.line: I don't have a bank account, so cashing checks and paying bills costs me extra.

sources.passage: Six percent of adults were "unbanked" in 2024
Thirteen percent of adults used nonbank check cashing or money orders in 2024.
Twenty-two percent of adults with income below $25,000 were unbanked

no-bank-account.prevalence: Six percent of U.S. adults were unbanked in 2024, and twenty-two percent of adults with income below $25,000 (Federal Reserve SHED).

credit-report-errors.name: Credit report
credit-report-errors.line: My credit report has mistakes I can't get fixed.

sources.passage: Consumers submitted more than 5.8 million credit or consumer reporting complaints, which accounted for 88% of those received
In 2025, the monthly average for the top issue, Incorrect information on your report, increased 249%

credit-report-errors.prevalence: More than 5.8 million credit reporting complaints reached the CFPB in 2025, 88% of all complaints; the top issue was incorrect information on the report.

debt-collectors.name: Debt collectors
debt-collectors.line: Debt collectors keep coming after me, sometimes for money I don't owe.

sources.passage: The CFPB received approximately 387,400 debt collection complaints in 2025.
the most common issue was Attempts to collect debt not owed

debt-collectors.prevalence: The CFPB received about 387,400 debt collection complaints in 2025; the most common issue was attempts to collect debt not owed.

identity-theft.name: Identity theft
identity-theft.line: Someone used my name to open accounts or take my money.

sources.passage: there were more than 1.1 million reports of identity theft received through the FTC's IdentityTheft.gov website.

identity-theft.prevalence: The FTC received more than 1.1 million identity theft reports in a single year (Consumer Sentinel).

supporting-family.name: Supporting family
supporting-family.line: I'm paying to support my parents or grown kids, and there isn't enough left for me.

sources.passage: Supporting parents/children/grandchildren 2 2 1 1 1 2

supporting-family.prevalence: 2% of U.S. adults named supporting parents, children or grandchildren as their family’s most important financial problem (Gallup, latest year).

insurance-costs.name: Insurance
insurance-costs.line: I can barely afford the insurance I need.

sources.passage: Insurance/Life insurance 2 3 3 1 -- 2
insurance systems, savings, social security, health systems, rights, family, work

insurance-costs.prevalence: 2% of U.S. adults named insurance as their family’s most important financial problem (Gallup, latest year). Max-Neef lists insurance systems under the need for protection.

money-skills.name: Money skills
money-skills.line: I never learned how to budget or manage money.
aliases: I can't keep track of where my money goes.

sources.passage: Each year, U.S. adults have correctly answered only about one-half of the 28 index questions, on average.
In 2026, this figure was 47%, and it has never exceeded 52%.
Controlling spending 1 * 1 * * *

money-skills.prevalence: U.S. adults answered 47% of 28 personal finance questions correctly in 2026, and never more than 52% in any year (TIAA Institute-GFLEC P-Fin Index).

sending-money-home.name: Sending money home
sending-money-home.line: I lose too much to fees when I send money to family in another country.

sources.passage: The global average cost of sending $200 was 6.7 per cent in the second quarter of 2024
By 2030, reduce to less than 3 per cent the transaction costs of migrant remittances

sending-money-home.prevalence: Sending $200 abroad cost 6.7 per cent on average, against an SDG target of 3 per cent (UN SDG report).

utility-bills.name: Utility bills
utility-bills.line: I'm behind on my power or water bill.

sources.passage: Utilities assistance was the second-largest referral category, increasing nearly 6% from 2024.
Energy costs/oil and gas prices 13 3 6 5 10 1

utility-bills.prevalence: Utilities were the second-largest referral category for the United Way helpline, up nearly 6% from 2024. 13% of U.S. adults named energy costs as their family’s top financial problem, up from 3% a year earlier (Gallup).

investments.name: Investments
investments.line: I worry my savings and investments will lose their value.

sources.passage: Not getting a good return on your investments 20 34 54 37
Stock market/investments 2 6 1 1 1 2

investments.prevalence: 54% of U.S. adults were very or moderately worried about not getting a good return on their investments (Gallup, latest year).
